description: Savor the rich flavors of Middle Eastern Lamb Ouzi, a delectable dish featuring tender lamb pieces and aromatic spiced rice. This recipe brings the essence of a traditional feast to your table, perfect for gatherings or a special family dinner. Each bite offers a harmonious blend of fragrant spices, succulent lamb, and fluffy rice, creating an unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb and Spices
instructions.text: In a bowl, toss the lamb shoulder cubes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon of nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon of cardamom, salt, and pepper. Ensure the lamb is evenly coated with the spices. If using pre-cooked lamb, simply season it now.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Sear Lamb
instructions.text: Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the seasoned lamb cubes and sear for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. This step is to build flavor quickly.

instructions.title: Cook the Rice with Lamb
instructions.text: Add the rinsed basmati rice to the pot with the lamb and onions. Stir in the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon of nutmeg, the ground cloves, and any remaining cardamom. Pour in the lamb or chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during this time.

instructions.title: Toast Nuts and Fluff Rice
instructions.text: While the rice is cooking, lightly toast the blanched almonds and pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown and fragrant. Once the rice is cooked, remove the pot from heat and let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes. Then, gently fluff the rice with a fork, incorporating the lamb pieces.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: Transfer the Lamb Ouzi rice mixture to a large serving platter. Arrange it beautifully, creating a mound in the center. This presentation makes the dish truly special for your guests.

instructions.title: Garnish and Enjoy
instructions.text: Generously sprinkle the toasted almonds and pine nuts over the Ouzi. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley for a burst of color and freshness. Serve immediately and enjoy this fragrant Middle Eastern delight as a centerpiece for your meal.

tips: For an even richer flavor, you can marinate the lamb cubes overnight with the spices and a touch of yogurt before cooking.
If you prefer a vegetarian option, replace the lamb with chickpeas and add more vegetables like carrots and peas to the rice.
Leftover Lamb Ouzi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave, adding a splash of broth if needed.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East with a dish that epitomizes grandeur, flavour, and communal celebration: Lamb Ouzi. This iconic feast, often reserved for special occasions and large gatherings, is a testament to the region's rich gastronomic heritage. While variations exist across different countries, the essence remains the same – incredibly tender, slow-roasted lamb, infused with aromatic spices, served atop a bed of fragrant, nutty rice pilaf. Preparing a whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is an act of love, patience, and tradition, promising an unforgettable dining experience that will transport your taste buds straight to a vibrant Middle Eastern dinner table. If you're looking to impress guests or simply indulge in a truly spectacular meal, mastering this recipe is a rewarding endeavour.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, sometimes spelled "Ozzy" or "Ozi," is a beloved and impressive dish originating from the Levant and Gulf regions of the Middle East. At its core, it's a magnificent presentation of slow-cooked lamb, traditionally a whole leg or shoulder, often presented dramatically over a mound of spiced rice. The name "Ouzi" itself can refer to the preparation style, particularly the slow roasting, and the combination of meat with rice and nuts. It’s more than just a meal; it's a centerpiece, a symbol of hospitality and abundance. The lamb is typically marinated with a blend of warming spices like cardamom, cinnamon, allspice, cumin, and coriander, which penetrate the meat during its long, slow roast, resulting in fall-off-the-bone tenderness and a depth of flavour that is truly unparalleled. The accompanying rice pilaf is equally important, usually basmati rice cooked with broth, onions, and a similar spice profile, often studded with green peas and toasted nuts like pine nuts, almonds, or pistachios, adding texture and richness.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

To create an authentic and show-stopping Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi, quality ingredients are key. This recipe focuses on a whole lamb leg or shoulder for maximum impact and flavour.

For the Lamb:
*   1 whole lamb leg or shoulder (bone-in, about 5-7 lbs / 2.5-3.5 kg)
*   1/4 cup olive oil
*   6-8 cloves garlic, minced
*   Juice of 1 large lemon
*   2 teaspoons salt
*   1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
*   1 tablespoon ground cumin
*   1 tablespoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon ground turmeric
*   1 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   1 teaspoon allspice
*   1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika (optional, for colour and depth)
*   Fresh rosemary or thyme sprigs (optional, for roasting pan)
*   1-2 cups chicken or vegetable broth (for the roasting pan)

For the Spiced Rice Pilaf:
*   3 cups basmati rice, rinsed thoroughly
*   1/4 cup ghee or unsalted butter
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   4-5 cups hot chicken or vegetable broth
*   1 teaspoon salt
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   Pinch of ground cloves (optional)
*   1 cup frozen green peas, thawed
*   1/2 cup toasted pine nuts
*   1/2 cup toasted slivered almonds
*   Fresh parsley or mint, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lamb Ouzi

Preparing this magnificent Lamb Ouzi requires patience, but the steps are straightforward and the result is incredibly rewarding.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb**: Pat the lamb leg or shoulder thoroughly dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the fatty side of the lamb in a diamond pattern, about 1/2 inch deep. In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, salt, pepper, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, allspice, and paprika. Rub this marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scores. For best results, place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavours to meld.
2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb**: Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a sturdy roasting pan. You can add a few sprigs of fresh rosemary or thyme and some chopped onions and carrots to the pan if desired, to add flavour to the pan drippings. Pour 1-2 cups of broth into the bottom of the pan. Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil (or use a roasting bag/lid if your pan has one). Roast for 4-6 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb. Halfway through, you can baste the lamb with the pan juices. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and crisp up slightly.
3.  **Rest the Lamb**: Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a carving board, and tent it loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving. This step is crucial for juicy, tender meat.
4.  **Prepare the Spiced Rice Pilaf**: While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the ghee or butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the rinsed basmati rice and toast it for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until slightly opaque. Stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, and optional cloves. Pour in the hot broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
5.  **Finish the Rice**: Once the rice is cooked, remove it from the heat and let it sit, covered, for another 10 minutes. Then, gently fluff the rice with a fork. Stir in the thawed green peas and half of the toasted pine nuts and slivered almonds.
6.  **Assemble and Serve**: Carve the slow-roasted lamb into large portions or shred it directly from the bone. On a large serving platter, create a mound of the fragrant spiced rice. Arrange the carved lamb over or around the rice. Garnish generously with the remaining toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley or mint.

## Pro Tips for the Best Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Achieving the perfect Lamb Ouzi means paying attention to a few key details that elevate the dish from good to unforgettable.

*   **Quality Lamb Matters**: Start with a high-quality, fresh lamb leg or shoulder. Bone-in lamb will always yield more flavour and moisture due to the marrow and connective tissues.
*   **Marination Time is Gold**: Do not rush the marination. Allowing the lamb to soak in the aromatic spices overnight truly infuses the meat with deep flavour and helps tenderize it.
*   **Low and Slow is the Way**: The secret to melt-in-your-mouth lamb is a low oven temperature and a long cooking time. This breaks down tough fibres, resulting in incredibly tender meat that easily pulls apart. Resist the urge to crank up the heat.
*   **Don't Forget to Rest**: After roasting, resting the lamb is non-negotiable. This allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring every bite is succulent and moist.
*   **Toast Your Nuts**: Toasting the pine nuts and almonds intensifies their flavour and adds a delightful crunch. Do this gently in a dry pan until lightly golden to avoid burning.
*   **Taste and Adjust**: Always taste your rice before serving and adjust seasoning if needed. The balance of spices is crucial for the overall harmony of the dish.
*   **Pan Juices**: The drippings in the roasting pan are liquid gold. Skim off excess fat and serve the rich pan juices alongside the lamb for an extra layer of flavour.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a complete meal in itself, a grand centrepiece designed to be enjoyed communally. However, a few accompaniments can enhance the experience and balance the richness of the dish.

*   **Yogurt Sauce (Laban)**: A simple, cooling yogurt sauce, perhaps with a hint of garlic and mint, provides a refreshing contrast to the rich lamb and spiced rice.
*   **Simple Green Salad**: A crisp, light salad with a tangy lemon vinaigrette can cut through the richness and add freshness.
*   **Fresh Pita Bread**: Warm pita bread is perfect for scooping up any remaining rice or sauce.
*   **Pickles (Torshi)**: Assorted Middle Eastern pickles offer a delightful sour and briny counterpoint.
*   **Herbs and Lemon Wedges**: Offer extra fresh herbs (parsley, mint) and lemon wedges for guests to add a final burst of flavour.

## Variations and Substitutions for Lamb Ouzi

While the classic Lamb Ouzi is a masterpiece, there are many ways to adapt it to your preferences or available ingredients.

*   **Different Cuts of Lamb**: If a whole leg is too large, you can use a bone-in lamb shoulder, lamb shanks, or even a boneless leg of lamb (adjust cooking time accordingly). For smaller gatherings, individual lamb shanks prepared in the same manner are also stunning.
*   **Spice Blends**: While specific spices are listed, Middle Eastern baharat spice mix is an excellent all-in-one alternative. Feel free to adjust the quantities of individual spices to suit your taste – more cardamom for a floral note, more cumin for earthiness.
*   **Rice Variations**: Basmati is traditional, but other long-grain rice varieties can be used. For a richer flavour, some recipes might include a layer of finely minced cooked ground lamb or beef mixed into the rice.
*   **Additional Toppings/Fillings**: Beyond pine nuts and almonds, consider adding toasted pistachios, dried cranberries or raisins for a touch of sweetness, or even sautéed chickpeas to the rice.
*   **Cooking Method for Lamb**: While slow roasting is ideal, the lamb can also be slow-cooked in a large pot or even a pressure cooker for a significantly reduced cooking time, though the oven roast provides that beautiful exterior browning.
*   **Vegetarian Ouzi**: For a vegetarian take, the spiced rice can be topped with large roasted portobello mushrooms, roasted seasonal vegetables (like eggplants, bell peppers, or zucchini), or even spiced lentils.

Preparing and sharing Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is more than just cooking; it’s an experience that celebrates tradition, flavour, and togetherness. This impressive Middle Eastern dinner recipe is sure to become a cherished part of your culinary repertoire, bringing joy and a taste of authentic Middle Eastern hospitality to your table.
